rationale: Same category, two spellings; leaving both would split every gender cut in two.

decision: Impute the median within employment_type; add years_employed_missing flag.
rationale: Tenure differs strongly by employment type, so a global median would be misleading. The target is never used.

decision: Impute the overall median; add num_dependents_missing flag.
rationale: Small integer count with no strong group structure.

decision: Impute the median within housing_type; add years_at_residence_missing flag.
rationale: Residence tenure depends on housing type (owners stay longer).

decision: Impute the median within loan_type; add interest_rate_missing flag.
rationale: Rates are tightly banded by product (e.g. cards 10-30 %, mortgages 4-9 %).

decision: Cap at max(age-16, 0); add years_employed_capped flag.
rationale: Nobody can have worked longer than their working-age life; capping keeps the row and the direction of the signal.

issue: Unemployed customers reporting income above the 12,000 floor used for all other unemployed
decision: Keep the values; add income_employment_conflict flag.
rationale: Income may be rental, benefits or family support. Changing it would be a guess; the flag lets analysts exclude them.

issue: Missing days_past_due on external credit lines
decision: Do NOT impute 0. Keep NaN, add dpd_reported flag; aggregate with max() over reported lines and count unreported lines.
rationale: Not reported is not the same as not late; imputing 0 would understate delinquency.

issue: Customers with no bureau lines at all (thin file)
decision: Keep via left join; counts become 0, ratios stay NaN; add no_bureau_file flag at account level.
rationale: Dropping them would lose ~10 % of customers and bias the portfolio; 'no history' is itself a risk signal.

issue: Loan originated before the customer relationship began
decision: Keep dates; add originated_before_customer_since flag; do NOT use customer_since or 'relationship age' as a feature.
rationale: About half of loans are affected, so the field is unreliable rather than a handful of typos. No way to know which date is right.

issue: Bureau lines opened after 2023-12-31 (later than every loan in the data); no snapshot date exists
decision: Keep; add opened_after_data_cutoff flag. Bureau fields are used as supplied; a point-in-time sensitivity run is reported in reports/metrics.json.
rationale: The bureau extract has no as-of date, so exact point-in-time features are impossible. The sensitivity run shows how much the result depends on this.

issue: Collections action dated before the loan was originated
decision: Keep for analytics; add event_before_origination flag; EXCLUDE collections data from the default model entirely.
rationale: Collections follow delinquency, so they are a consequence of the target; their dates cannot be ordered against the loan timeline.

issue: action_type 'SMS/Email Notice' is called 'SMS-Email' in DATA_DICTIONARY.md
decision: Keep the label in the data; documented here.
rationale: The data is the source of truth; renaming would break joins to anything built on the raw file.

issue: Observation window: every account has exactly months 1..12, even 360-month mortgages
decision: Observation point = end of month 12; all repayment features use months 1..12 only.
rationale: No default date or snapshot date exists. This definition is explicit and applied uniformly, so no feature can see beyond it.
